done.why: I had seen the opening stretch and the best trick, the Wizard's illusion. I stopped at the garden's southern edge without reaching an ending.

about: A Zork II style cave adventure. You start in a barrow with a lamp and an Elvish sword, then cross a cavern and a garden. A wizard wanders in and casts words that conjure illusions, such as a basilisk that isn't there.

moments.note: The Wizard appeared and cast Fantasize. I couldn't repeat the word myself.
Examining the basilisk revealed it was an illusion, and the room looked embarrassed about it.
The unicorn vanished and reappeared. Commands naming it failed with 'can't see any such thing'.
Some of my odd phrasings got a stock 'sentence isn't one I recognize' reply.

wished: Interact with the unicorn and the sword's glow.

lines.line: The room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: Funny, and it explains the illusion.

lines.line: I don't think that the lamp would agree with you.

fun.why: A few good moments, but my short session was mostly walking.

engagement.why: The illusion mystery drew me in, and I stopped before it developed.

difficulty.why: There was nothing blocking me in the stretch I played.

interestingness.why: Familiar Zork geography with a new illusion twist.

prose.why: The prose is witty, with the Zork voice intact.
